subproblem.title: Simon 2.5 bound: |δV(Y)| ≤ sup|Y| · ‖δV‖(W) for test fields supported in W ⊂⊂ U
subproblem.statement: Let V be an n-varifold on the open set U ⊆ ℝ^N with locally bounded first variation, let W ⊆ ℝ^N be open with closure W compact and closure W ⊆ U, let K ∈ ℝ, and let Y : ℝ^N → ℝ^N be a C¹ vector field with tsupport Y ⊆ W and |Y(z)| ≤ K for all z. Then |δV(Y)| ≤ K·‖δV‖(W), where δV(Y) = V.firstVariation Y and ‖δV‖ = variationMeasure V; in ℝ≥0∞: ofReal|δV(Y)| ≤ ofReal K · variationMeasure V W.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclidean N)) (V : Varifold N n U) (W : Set (Euclidean N)) (Y : Euclidean N → Euclidean N) (K : ℝ), V.HasLocallyBoundedFirstVariation → IsOpen W → IsCompact (closure W) → closure W ⊆ U → ContDiff ℝ 1 Y → tsupport Y ⊆ W → (∀ z, ‖Y z‖ ≤ K) → ENNReal.ofReal |V.firstVariation Y| ≤ ENNReal.ofReal K * variationMeasure V W
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 5–6 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 8, 2.5, p. 209: ‖δV‖(W) = sup{|δV(X)| : X ∈ K(U;ℝ^N), |X| ≤ 1, spt X ⊆ W} for open W ⊂⊂ U, kernel-checked as SimonGMT Varifold.firstVariationRieszMeasure_eq_norm, FirstVariationRiesz.lean:218). Notation: δV(Y) := V.firstVariation Y; ‖δV‖ := variationMeasure V; hV : V.HasLocallyBoundedFirstVariation.
1. (Y is a test field.) tsupport Y ⊆ W ⊆ closure W. Since tsupport Y is closed and contained in the compact set closure W, it is compact, i.e. HasCompactSupport Y (IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset). Also tsupport Y ⊆ closure W ⊆ U. Hence Y together with its C¹ property is an element Y' of Varifold.TestVectorField U.
2. (‖δV‖(W) is the supremum of 2.5.) By the definition of variationMeasure and hV (dif_pos, equivalently dite_eq_left), variationMeasure V = V.firstVariationRieszMeasure hV. As W is open with closure W compact and contained in U, Varifold.firstVariationRieszMeasure_eq_norm gives V.firstVariationRieszMeasure hV W = V.firstVariationNormOn W. Hence variationMeasure V W = V.firstVariationNormOn W, and it suffices to prove ofReal|δV(Y)| ≤ ofReal K · V.firstVariationNormOn W.
3. (K ≥ 0.) 0 ≤ ‖Y 0‖ ≤ K.
4. (Case K = 0.) Then ‖Y z‖ ≤ 0, so Y z = 0 for every z, i.e. Y is the zero field, and Varifold.firstVariation_zero gives δV(Y) = 0. The left side is ofReal|0| = 0, which is ≤ the right side.
5. (Case K > 0: normalization.) Let Ŷ := K⁻¹•Y, i.e. Ŷ = Y'.scale K⁻¹ ∈ TestVectorField U. Then tsupport Ŷ ⊆ tsupport Y ⊆ W (TestVectorField.tsupport_scale_subset) and ‖Ŷ z‖ = K⁻¹‖Y z‖ ≤ K⁻¹·K = 1 for every z. So Ŷ.UnitSupportedIn W. Since V.firstVariationNormOn W is by definition the supremum over all test fields X of (ofReal|δV(X)| if X.UnitSupportedIn W, else 0), Varifold.le_firstVariationNormOn gives ofReal|δV(Ŷ)| ≤ V.firstVariationNormOn W.
6. (Linearity.) Y is C¹ with compact support, so Varifold.firstVariation_const_smul gives δV(K⁻¹•Y) = K⁻¹·δV(Y); as K⁻¹ > 0, |δV(Ŷ)| = K⁻¹·|δV(Y)|.
7. (Conclusion.) |δV(Y)| = K·(K⁻¹·|δV(Y)|), so by ENNReal.ofReal_mul (K ≥ 0) ofReal|δV(Y)| = ofReal K · ofReal(K⁻¹·|δV(Y)|) = ofReal K · ofReal|δV(Ŷ)| ≤ ofReal K · V.firstVariationNormOn W = ofReal K · variationMeasure V W, by step 5, monotonicity of multiplication in ℝ≥0∞, and step 2. ∎
proof_key_steps: tsupport Y ⊆ W ⊆ closure W (compact, ⊆ U), so Y is a TestVectorField U with compact support.
variationMeasure V W = firstVariationRieszMeasure hV W = firstVariationNormOn W (dif_pos and firstVariationRieszMeasure_eq_norm).
K ≥ 0; if K = 0 then Y = 0 and δV(Y) = 0.
If K > 0, Ŷ = K⁻¹Y is UnitSupportedIn W, so ofReal|δV(Ŷ)| ≤ firstVariationNormOn W (le_firstVariationNormOn).
δV(Ŷ) = K⁻¹δV(Y) (firstVariation_const_smul) and ofReal_mul give ofReal|δV(Y)| ≤ ofReal K · variationMeasure V W.

Local bounded first variation and the stated conditions on W justify the Riesz-norm identification. The proof derives K ≥ 0, handles K = 0, and for K > 0 correctly normalizes Y, applies the defining supremum bound, and restores the scale using homogeneity and ENNReal multiplication. It is complete, non-circular, and ready for formalization. The bare name is unreserved.

subproblem.title: First variation of the rescaling V_{x,t}: change of variables for the divergence integral
subproblem.statement: Let U ⊆ ℝ^N, let V be an n-varifold on U (V : Varifold N n U; no bounded-first-variation, support or integrability hypothesis is needed), x ∈ ℝ^N, t > 0, and X : ℝ^N → ℝ^N a C¹ vector field. Put ψ(z) := t⁻¹(z − x) and Y(z) := t·X(ψ(z)). Then ∫ div_S X(y) dV_{x,t}(y,S) = (t⁻¹)^n·δV(Y), where V_{x,t} = rescaledMeasure V x t = ofReal((t⁻¹)^n)·(V.measure).map((z,S) ↦ (ψ z, S)), div_S X(y) = Varifold.tangentialDivergence X y S = trace(S·jacobian X y), and δV(Y) = V.firstVariation Y = ∫ div_S Y(z) dV(z,S) (all integrals are Bochner integrals; the identity holds as such).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclidean N)) (V : Varifold N n U) (x : Euclidean N) (t : ℝ) (X : Euclidean N → Euclidean N), 0 < t → ContDiff ℝ 1 X → ∫ z, Varifold.tangentialDivergence X z.1 z.2 ∂(rescaledMeasure V x t) = t⁻¹ ^ n * V.firstVariation (fun z : Euclidean N ↦ t • X (t⁻¹ • (z - x)))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1–3 of the parent proof (fact R2; Simon Ch. 8, §5, p. 215, rescalings η_{x,λ#}V of 5.1–5.2). Notation: ψ(z) := t⁻¹•(z − x); φ(z,S) := (ψ z, S); f(w,S) := div_S X(w) := Varifold.tangentialDivergence X w S = trace(S·jacobian X w), where jacobian X w is the coordinate matrix of fderiv ℝ X w; Y(z) := t•X(ψ z); δV(Y) := V.firstVariation Y = ∫ div_S Y(z) dV.measure(z,S).
1. (Derivative of the pulled-back field.) Fix w ∈ ℝ^N. The map z ↦ z − x has derivative Id at w, so ψ has derivative t⁻¹•Id at w (HasFDerivAt.sub_const, HasFDerivAt.const_smul). X is C¹, hence differentiable at ψ(w), with derivative D := fderiv ℝ X (ψ w). By the chain rule (HasFDerivAt.comp), X∘ψ has derivative D∘(t⁻¹•Id) at w, and Y = t•(X∘ψ) has derivative t•(D∘(t⁻¹•Id)) at w (HasFDerivAt.const_smul). For every v, (t•(D∘(t⁻¹•Id)))(v) = t•D(t⁻¹•v) = (t·t⁻¹)•D(v) = D(v), because t ≠ 0. Hence fderiv ℝ Y w = fderiv ℝ X (ψ w) (HasFDerivAt.fderiv).
2. (Pointwise divergence identity.) By step 1, jacobian Y w = jacobian X (ψ w) for every w, so for every (z,S): div_S Y(z) = trace(S·jacobian Y z) = trace(S·jacobian X (ψ z)) = div_S X(ψ z) = f(φ(z,S)).
3. (Scalar factor.) By definition, rescaledMeasure V x t = c • (V.measure.map φ) with c := ofReal((t⁻¹)^n). For every function g and every measure μ, ∫ g d(c•μ) = c.toReal • ∫ g dμ (integral_smul_measure; no integrability hypothesis is needed). Since t > 0, (t⁻¹)^n ≥ 0, so c.toReal = (t⁻¹)^n (ENNReal.toReal_ofReal). Thus ∫ f d(rescaledMeasure V x t) = (t⁻¹)^n · ∫ f d(V.measure.map φ).
4. (Pushforward.) φ is continuous (its components (z,S) ↦ t⁻¹•(z − x) and (z,S) ↦ S are continuous), hence measurable; f is continuous (Varifold.continuous_tangentialDivergence, as X is C¹), hence AE-strongly measurable with respect to V.measure.map φ. Therefore integral_map gives ∫ f d(V.measure.map φ) = ∫ f(φ(z,S)) dV.measure(z,S), again without any integrability hypothesis.
5. (Conclusion.) By step 2 the integrands f∘φ and (z,S) ↦ div_S Y(z) agree everywhere, so ∫ f∘φ dV.measure = ∫ div_S Y(z) dV.measure(z,S) = V.firstVariation Y (definition of Varifold.firstVariation). Combining steps 3–5: ∫ div_S X dV_{x,t} = (t⁻¹)^n · V.firstVariation Y, i.e. ∫ z, Varifold.tangentialDivergence X z.1 z.2 ∂(rescaledMeasure V x t) = t⁻¹ ^ n * V.firstVariation (fun z ↦ t • X (t⁻¹ • (z − x))). ∎
proof_key_steps: Chain rule: D(t·X∘ψ)(w) = t·DX(ψ w)∘(t⁻¹·Id) = DX(ψ w), so jacobian Y w = jacobian X (ψ w).
Pointwise identity div_S Y(z) = div_S X(ψ z) for all (z,S).
integral_smul_measure with toReal(ofReal((t⁻¹)^n)) = (t⁻¹)^n pulls out the scalar factor.
integral_map (φ continuous, integrand continuous) turns the pushforward integral into ∫ div_S X(ψ z) dV(z,S).
That integral equals ∫ div_S Y dV = δV(Y), giving ∫ div_S X dV_{x,t} = (t⁻¹)^n·δV(Y).

The proof correctly cancels the derivative factors t and t⁻¹, obtains the pointwise divergence identity, and applies integral_smul_measure and integral_map. The latter requires measurability, not integrability, so the stronger total-Bochner statement is justified. C¹ regularity supplies the required continuity. Scalar operations infer the intended real and Euclidean instances; no problematic matrix-unit construction occurs. The bare name is unreserved.
